claim_verdicts.evidence: Kanban has no versions.yaml key; judged against glossary wip-limit ('A cap on how many items can sit in one column at once; once full, something must finish before more starts') and The Kanban Guide (May 2025, via WebFetch summary): 'Any work items between a started point and a finished point are considered work in progress (WIP).' 'Kanban system members should refrain from selecting more than the number of work items into a given part of the workflow beyond the WIP control.' A column is one such part.

git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:docs/team/kanban-board-example.md: line 8 header 'Đang làm (giới hạn 2) | Chờ review (giới hạn 2)'; lines 10-11 put two items in Đang làm (Dev 3, Dev 2), one in Chờ review (Dev 1). Lines 16-20: 'Dev 4 vừa xong một việc và định lấy việc thứ ba ... Trưởng nhóm chặn lại ... Một cột đầy là tín hiệu tắc nghẽn, không phải chỗ trống cho người rảnh.' Both code blocks match lines 8-12 and 16-20 verbatim.

The Kanban Guide (WebFetch summary): 'Controlling WIP helps flow and often improves the Kanban system members' collective focus, commitment, and collaboration.' and 'When WIP drops below the control set in the DoW, that can be a signal to select new work.' (start only when something finishes). Bottleneck visibility: the Guide does not use the word; supported by the repo file line 19 'Một cột đầy là tín hiệu tắc nghẽn'. Lesson words it as a mechanism, not a guarantee; acceptable.

From the board at stage-1 lines 10-12: Đang làm 2 items / limit 2; Chờ review 1 / limit 2. Step 2: review item to Xong -> Chờ review 0/2, two places, Đang làm unchanged 2/2. Step 3 (alternative): product page fix to Chờ review (file line 34: 'sang "Chờ review" khi pull request mở') -> Chờ review 2/2 (allowed, was 1/2), Đang làm 1/2. Arithmetic in §7 Expected result matches.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: an empirical throughput statement presented as the sign of the misconception. Not in the claims ledger, and not supported as a general fact: The Kanban Guide only says controlling WIP 'helps flow and often improves' focus; it makes no claim that more open items means fewer finished per week. What reliably changes with too much open work is how long each item takes to finish.
issues.quote: You notice this when a team with many items open at once finishes fewer of them each week than it did with a limit.
issues.fix: Replace with: "You notice this when a team with many items open at once sees each one take longer to reach `Xong`, even though everyone is busy." Add it to claims as kind opinion/fact with source_hint The Kanban Guide ('Controlling WIP helps flow').

issues.text: Unlisted claim about general convention ('usually'). Neither the glossary nor The Kanban Guide states how WIP limits are usually written; the Guide only requires WIP to be explicitly controlled. Only this repo's board is evidence (number in parentheses after the column name).
issues.quote: A **WIP limit** is written on a column, usually as a number next to its name.
issues.fix: Replace with: "A **WIP limit** is written on a column; on the support team's board it is the number in brackets after the column name." Or keep the sentence and add it to the claims ledger with a source.

issues.text: The suggested answer says helping the waiting review is what frees the place, but in the lesson's own step 3 the place in Đang làm was freed by the product page fix moving to Chờ review, which already had room (1 of 2). Reviewing did not free that place.
issues.quote: helping move an existing item forward, such as the review waiting in `Chờ review`, is what frees a place in the first place.
issues.fix: Replace with: "helping move existing items forward, such as the review waiting in `Chờ review`, is how places free up; here the place came when the product page fix moved on."

issues.fix: In §5 write: "wants to take a third item from `Việc cần làm` into `Đang làm`", matching §2 and §7.
